reason: In the 'password not provided / empty' branch (lines 48-50), the code does session_uid = get_session_id(config, request); then immediately calls j_result = get_users_for_session(config, session_uid) WITHOUT any NULL check on session_uid. Per the verified definition in src/session.c:630-636, get_session_id returns NULL whenever the cookie is missing or its length != GLEWLWYD_SESSION_ID_LENGTH (return NULL; line 634). Thus an attacker can trigger this path simply by POSTing {"username":"x"} with no valid session cookie. Critically, this SAME function elsewhere guards exactly this NULL case: line 20-22 does 'if ((session_uid = get_session_id(...)) == NULL) session_uid = generate_session_id();' and line 37 does '(session_uid = get_session_id(...)) != NULL && user_session_update(...)'. Additionally, other call sites of get_users_for_session (webservice.c:641 and 2360) wrap it in 'if (session_uid != NULL && o_strlen(session_uid))'. This asymmetry — the identical get_session_id call is NULL-guarded at lines 20/37 but not at line 49-50 — is the classic signature of the CVE-2016-8652 pattern (auth crash when a value is unexpectedly NULL, strlen/deref on NULL). Passing NULL into get_users_for_session (which internally hashes/uses session_uid at session.c:~214 generate_hash) yields a NULL-pointer dereference / DoS reachable by unauthenticated remote request.

src/webservice.c:641 / 2360: if (session_uid != NULL && o_strlen(session_uid)) { j_session = get_users_for_session(config, session_uid); ... } —— 其它调用点对同一函数均判空，说明 NULL 调用不安全
